question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose plugin-declared AI-safety emission permissions and durable operator-readable safety history as a core product contract?
rationale: This changes the plugin SDK and manifest contract while introducing session-linked persisted diagnostics and a new operator query surface; implementation review cannot safely choose the permanent privacy, retention, compatibility, and ownership policy.

options.title: Pause for a core contract decision
options.body: Do not merge until an owner approves the permanent plugin API, manifest capability semantics, privacy/redaction rules, retention, and operator-access model.

options.title: Narrow the first phase
options.body: Keep the work internal to core diagnostics and exporters, deferring external plugin emission, durable history, and UI/CLI operator surfaces until their contracts are separately sponsored.

options.title: Approve the full surface
options.body: Accept the plugin and storage contract as proposed, then require focused compatibility, retention, and end-to-end proof before landing.

recommendation.title: Pause for a core contract decision
recommendation.body: Do not merge until an owner approves the permanent plugin API, manifest capability semantics, privacy/redaction rules, retention, and operator-access model.

likelyOwner.reason: Skoya authored the canonical request and the current implementation, so they are the best available discussion contact; a repository owner must make the final product decision.
